title: Local quant eval lineage and deterministic-seed mapping notes
body:
Purpose and quick summary:

This is a personal scratchpad for a compact, developer-facing local evaluation harness for quantized model variants. Goal: make it trivial for a dev to run deterministic micro-benchmarks and quality checks on quantized artifacts, produce lineage-traceable results, and generate small reproducible manifests that can be promoted to CI/evals.

Why we need this (pain points):
- Current eval flows in CI are heavyweight and non-deterministic across machines (different BLAS/GPU drivers -> different rounding).
- Hard to trace which quantization pass + seed + kernel selection produced a surprising BLEU/ROUGE/regression.
- Manual steps to snapshot artifacts and link to results lead to lost context when debugging regressions.

Primary constraints and non-goals:
- Not a full-blown infra project. Lightweight, runs on a developer laptop or small cloud instance.
- Should work for CPU-quantized artifacts (int8/4-bit) and small GPU runs with stable kernels. Not aiming to solve cross-driver nondeterminism fully.
- Not a replacement for Redwood Optimize; intended as a dev-first complement to iterate quickly before CI.

User stories:
- "Maya" wants to run quantize -> eval on a small prompt set, fix quant params, and re-run, with an easy way to compare runs and produce a compact manifest to attach to a PR.
- "Priya" wants to re-run someone else's failing run: check out a small manifest, fetch artifact hash, and reproduce exact eval including RNG seeds and compiler flags.
- "Diego" wants to generate a single-line provenance tag that gets printed in CI so regression alerts can point back to the dev manifest.

Core design ideas (high level):
1) Deterministic seed mapping: every random source (quantizer dithering, calibration sample shuffle, eval sampling) gets named seeds derived from a single run-seed using a stable keyed-hash (HMAC-SHA256). This avoids global RNG bleed and documents deterministic inputs.
2) Artifact hashing and small index: each quantized artifact has a short content-addressed id (sha256 truncated to 12 chars) plus metadata: model-arch, quant-pass, tool-version, compiler flags. Store as local artifact registry (~.rq/artifacts.jsonl) for quick lookup.
3) Manifest format: single-line JSONL manifest per run with stable fields: run_id, run_seed, artifact_id, eval_suite_id, dataset_commit, platform-hints (cpu/gpu, kernel-version), env-hash, metrics. Keep small and attachable to GitHub PRs.
4) CLI-first UX: minimal commands: rq init, rq quantize --profile fast, rq eval --manifest X, rq compare runA runB, rq promote --to-ci.

Proposed CLI flags and shapes:
- rq init --repo-root . --profile dev
- rq quantize --input ../weights --profile small-int8 --seed 42 --calib-samples 512 --out ./artifacts
- rq eval --artifact ./artifacts/mymod-int8-0x23a --suite quick-chat --samples 200 --seed 420 --out run.jsonl
- rq compare runA.jsonl runB.jsonl --diff-metrics=perplexity,accuracy --output diff.md

Manifest schema (compact, single-line JSONL) - example (note: shown here as pretty JSON for readability in the doc; actual file is JSONL):
{
  "run_id": "rq-20260310-57c1",
  "run_seed": "20260310:seed:0xdeadbeef",
  "artifact_id": "a1b2c3d4e5f6",
  "artifact_meta": "int8+sym;quant-tool=v0.9.1;arch=llama-7b",
  "eval_suite": "quick-chat-200",
  "dataset_commit": "gh:dataset/conv-v1@f3a9",
  "platform_hint": "cpu-avx2;kernels=mkldnn-2.4",
  "env_hash": "pip:torch1.14|cudnn:---|gcc:11.3",
  "metrics": "ppl=12.3;acc@1=0.67",
  "notes": "calib-samples=512;calib-mode=per-channel"
}

On-disk layout (developer laptop):
~/repo/
  .rq/
    artifacts.jsonl           # catalog of local artifacts (one JSONL per artifact)
    runs.jsonl                # run manifests appended (single-line entries)
    cache/                    # optional cached tokenizer/model shards
  artifacts/                 # local outputs from quantize
  tests/evals/quick-chat/    # small eval prompt sets

Artifact JSONL example (single line)
{"artifact_id":"a1b2c3d4e5f6","created_at":"2026-03-10T14:22:00Z","source_weights":"gh:weights/llama-7b@c123","quant_pass":"sym-int8-perchannel","tool_version":"quantify-0.9.1","file_path":"artifacts/mymod-int8-0x23a","size_bytes":"81234567"}

Deterministic seed mapping sketch (pseudo):
function derive_seed(master_seed, name) {
  // name: e.g. "calib.shuffle" or "eval.sampling"
  key = HMAC_SHA256(master_seed, name)
  return last_8_bytes_as_u64(key) // stable mapping across platforms
}

Where we still get nondeterminism (notes):
- MKL/OpenBLAS floating-point ordering differences when running calibration on CPU. Recommend a default fallback: run calibration with single-thread or set OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 for reproducibility.
- GPU kernels: quantized GPU backends may produce small FP differences; document platform hints in manifest so CI can match the same driver.

Integrations and promotion path to CI:
- rq promote --to-ci should translate the local manifest into a CI job label (e.g. CI-EVAL-<run_id>) and upload artifact to a small S3 staging bucket with the artifact_id as key. CI jobs read the manifest and re-run with provided seeds.
- For security: artifacts uploaded to staging should be signed with developer's key (GPG or GitHub Actions OIDC signature) to avoid accidental mismatches.

Example quick workflow (commands):
1) rq init
2) rq quantize --input weight-path --profile small-int8 --seed 12345
3) rq eval --artifact ./artifacts/* --suite quick-chat --seed 12345 --out runs.jsonl
4) rq compare runs.jsonl:latest runs.jsonl:previous
5) rq promote --to-ci --note "regression-investigation"

Diff and visualization: keep diff output human-friendly (markdown): summary line with metric deltas, ASCII sparkbars for small metrics, link to artifact ids, and a compact mini-table that CI bots can parse.

Thoughts on API shapes for SDK (python):
- from rq import LocalHarness
- harness = LocalHarness(path='.', profile='dev')
- art = harness.quantize(weights_path, profile='small-int8', seed=seed)
- run = harness.eval(art, suite='quick-chat-200', seed=seed)
- harness.compare(run_a, run_b)

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide whether artifact ids should be fully content-addressed (sha256 over bytes) or include a short human-friendly slug for easier PR discussion. Tradeoff: content-addressed is unambiguous; slug is readable. Maybe both (id + slug).
- Should manifests include full env reproducibility (container -> yes/no)? For now include env-hash and a pointer to a container image in CI promote step.
- Add small web viewer (local) to render runs.jsonl with diff UI (later).
- Validate how much of this dovetails with Redwood Optimize suggestions and whether manifest fields should interop with Optimize metadata.

Notes to self:
- Ask @Liam about permission model for uploading dev artifacts to staging S3 (we need a small short-lived token/bucket with strict lifecycle).
- Check CONFLUENCE-1234 for existing eval-suite naming conventions.

References / links (scratch):
- jira: JIRA-EVAL-88 (design spike for local dev harness)
- github PR: github.com/redwood-inference/quant-eval-harness/pull/19 (proto CLI)
- slack: #eng-quant (thread ts=167xxx)

If I come back to this tomorrow:
- write a minimal python impl for derive_seed and validate identical outputs across mac/linux (docker-run).
- prototype rq show-run --open to open local markdown diff in $EDITOR or browser.

End of notes.
